catalogueTitle: Headline speaker needs to leave earlier; organiser previews consequences
note: Grace Nakamura (ait-draft-04, NRT origin, Day 1 future-provocation keynote 12:10-12:20) must depart SIN by ~10:30 on 1 Oct for an unavoidable external commitment in Tokyo; her booked outbound leaves 19:45. The organiser asks Northstar to preview moving her commitment earlier so she can take the 13:30 outbound — but the engine must run a counterfactual PREVIEW first, not mutate the event. The preview candidate swaps future-provocation with marketplace-chat (09:50-10:10): Grace becomes viable, interviewer Daniel Ong (ait-draft-02, local) remains viable, but marketplace speaker Lucas Ferreira (ait-draft-20) becomes disrupted because his booked same-day return SIN->SGN departs 12:30 — the displaced 12:10-12:30 slot collides with his outbound, forcing a traveller-funded or approval-bound rebook (~SGD 95). Transfer assumptions also change (Grace's departure transfer brought forward; Lucas's departure transfer invalidated). Simulated seam: no provider calls in S3; the preview artifact is pack-authored NATIVE_UI material describing the counterfactual the engine must reproduce deterministically.

affectedTravellers.reason: Moved slot 09:50-10:10 lets her leave the venue ~10:20 and make the 13:30 SIN->NRT outbound.

Marketplace-chat displaced to 12:10-12:30 collides with his booked same-day return MN231 (SIN->SGN, departs 12:30); recovery requires rebooking onto the 18:10 service with fare delta ~SGD 95 and approval.
Marketplace interviewer is local (Singapore) and free all day; the slot move only changes his morning sequencing.

expectedReasoningHooks: Preview-before-commit: the event mutation must exist only in an overlay/counterfactual until the operator explicitly commits; authoritative state is untouched.

AnchorEvent -> Trip propagation: a commitment time change fans out to every traveller with an engagement bound to the moved commitments (future-provocation, marketplace-chat), including outbound-flight collisions, not just arrival checks.
Counterfactual blast radius across 3 travellers with differentiated outcomes (viable / disrupted / unchanged); 'before changing the programme, know whose trip you are about to break'.

Strategy comparison: (a) programme swap only — zero event spend, one other traveller disrupted (Lucas rebook ~SGD 95); (b) rebook Grace's outbound to 13:30 — fare delta ~SGD 180, no programme impact; (c) leave unchanged — Grace misses her external commitment.

A programme-level change may solve the problem without purchasing travel for Grace, but the preview must expose that it purchases disruption for Lucas; the engine must not silently prefer one strategy.
